correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and each weak unimodal mode k, shortening a maximizing ball by two boundary values during a one-step move toward the peak cannot lower its mean: each removed value is no larger than the original central value, which is no larger than the original maximal average. The reverse argument after k proves unimodality of Mf. The peak value is exactly H, giving Var(Mf)=2H-Mf(1)-Mf(n). Prefix/suffix ball averages prove distinct endpoint gains (H-a)/k and (H-b)/(n-k+1). Thus the location bound and sharp global factor follow algebraically. Single spikes attain the two endpoint gains at each k; endpoint spikes attain 1-1/n. Exact rational verification passed 4332 exhaustive, 4800 deterministic longer, 5047 spike tests. Finite verification is not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: A complete public monotone-data theorem and primary maximal-function papers were compared at the level of hypotheses, operator, and conclusions. The new all-n unimodal result treats genuine interior peaks and a sharp quantified mode-dependent loss, neither implied by the monotone-data theorem nor by integer-line indicator/positive-fixed-point contraction. The 2026 full-path counterpart remains an explicit conjecture. Search absence is not treated as novelty proof; possible unpublished/folklore equivalent remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The elementary trimming lemma or the unimodal finite-path inequality may have appeared as unpublished folklore or in an unindexed treatment.
The larger original source manuscripts were inspected materially for their relevant theorem statements, not formally audited line by line in full.
The proof does not settle arbitrary oscillatory data; the 2026 conjecture must not be treated as established.

value.rationale: Genuinely one-peaked input is the first natural nonmonotone class of the open finite-path centered maximal variation conjecture. The result proves the conjectured sharp global constant uniformly in n on that class, establishes an analytic mode-preservation principle despite radius switching, and gives a location-sensitive strict deficit with simultaneous sharp spike witnesses. This is a motivated infinite-family boundary and not a numerical small-n extension, renaming, or known-table recomputation.
